scope: Brief reading summaries of current final.md; not replacement chapters

summaries.summary: Shrinking frames, multiplying rings and subdivided cubes separate a rule’s continuation from the limits of computation, visibility and bodily passage.
Branching trees change reach, connections and shelter through different procedures, asking what their convincing resemblance to living trees leaves out.
Repeated removal multiplies pieces while reducing material; gaps become passages only when their dimensions and solidity admit the visitor’s body.
Growing boundaries, removed triangles and changing measurements ask what a construction retains, what its display reveals and what its counting procedure misses.
A perforated cube offers flight through its largest openings, exposing the difference between geometric connection and a passage a particular body can use.
Fibonacci towers and a divided rectangle show how numerical relations acquire visible form through mappings that make some comparisons easier and others misleading.
Intervals and trees return as distinct procedures, asking which inherited rules, histories and representations would need to change to make room for another body.
The same rewritten sentence produces different drawings through different readers, revealing how interpretation, fitting and finite budgets shape the bodies a grammar can show.
A branching line saves and restores its travelling state, asking what a dependable return remembers and what its resemblance to a living tree omits.
A sentence turns sideways under another reader, while inherited tubes become connections and ceilings, asking how an instruction or line acquires consequences.
A branching plan acquires rooms and walls, making clear that connected lines do not guarantee passages wide enough for a particular body.
Identical trees draw unequal resources from shared soil, showing how turn order and seasonal rules distribute growth beyond what their branching instructions specify.
Tree controls sometimes change a number without changing a branch, revealing thresholds, drawing limits and desired forms the available controls cannot express.
Selected cube faces become projecting families and open canopies, asking which desired forms require new operations and what should remain open around a body.
Two marks invite paths across a textile, separating the generator’s choices from the viewer’s connections and the further work needed to make passages.
Generated boxes gain or lose their claim to be best when the target changes, while an uncounted ring exposes what the evaluator overlooks.
Branches answer attraction points under changing eligibility rules, showing how who may respond shapes a tree and which requests remain unmet.
Growth follows each site’s nearest invitation, but multiple child records can occupy one place, questioning what a branch count actually says about space.
Flow accepts face neighbours but ignores touching corners, making connection a stated rule whose success does not establish a route for bodies.
Carved caves and a backtracking maze reveal authored restrictions inside random generation, asking whether a proven array route gives shoulders and heads enough room.
Falling cubes become a sampled surface and cutters hollow a dome, exposing how chosen representations preserve, enlarge or erase openings and physical events.
Copied cellular patterns and changing tunnel networks separate image symmetry from connection, asking what independent differences and bodily access their surfaces conceal.
A pinned cube yields while a driven mill meets a soft sphere, asking how material, supports and unequal contact determine what can give way.
Hanging strips survive the removal of their apparent support, while released pins and added loads expose whose movement an arrangement permits or requires.
Hanging bodies respond to a driven carousel that cannot feel their response, asking which relations allow motion and which prescribe it.
Pinned walls swell under changing pressure, bringing softness into the architecture and asking how much room its breathing resemblance leaves for a visitor.
An array of soft-body falls holds unlike encounters together, asking which differences come from contact, settings or computation rather than their persuasive names.
A deforming body follows a partial measurement while a glass vessel freezes a chosen duration, asking what becomes invisible when an event becomes form.
Spiked and lattice forms invite recognition as living things, then expose the gap between biological resemblance, geometric recipes and any capacity to respond.
A seeded chemical field develops different patterns under different rates, asking what further mapping would turn pattern formation into a body or support.
A folded surface changes passages under a control called entropy, asking which bundled choices alter appearance, connection and room for a body.
A sampled noise field becomes a triangular boundary, asking which openings depend on the chosen level, which on resolution and which admit a body.
Eight corner values select and position a local surface, exposing the conventions and unresolved connections hidden behind a seemingly continuous boundary.
One extractor makes chairs and hollow cups from different fields, asking where recognition outruns sampling, preserved features or suitability for use.
A ring and repeating folded field distinguish visible openings from a limited capsule test, asking what the same surface permits for different bodies.
Rounded deposits merge and cuts alter their recorded history, asking how blending, gesture order, sampling and forgotten contributions shape what remains.
Hills acquire undersides and interior gaps when their description gains a volume, asking why additional detail alone cannot supply another kind of space.
Overlapping field contributions suggest arches without drawing doorways, asking where names and expectations exceed the openings and usable room the surface actually provides.
Buried rings and enclosing cave walls turn boundaries into possible interiors, asking whether their openings meet the floor and give a visitor adequate clearance.
Two caves reveal different generated conditions, asking who chose their possible passages and why one attractive opening cannot establish a generator’s accessibility.
Blocks appear and disappear as a field is resampled, questioning the persistent travelling objects our eyes invent from successive boundary approximations.
Local sources form shared necks through different field and display methods, asking which relation creates a join and which representation can let it separate.
A smoothly joined body appears through a bounded search along viewing rays, exposing how visible solidity can exist without a surface the hand encounters.
A chamber network invites a different return route, asking whether the cycles promised by its graph survive as passages a visitor can actually use.
Boxes and spheres keep, share or cut regions, asking whose remainder survives and why removal can create the place another body needs.
Neighbouring Boolean variants expose defaults, traces and scars, asking how presentation and catalogue order influence which forms seem ordinary or worth keeping.
Large hollows, walls and dark cavities offer different invitations, asking when a visible opening becomes a supported passage, a refuge or only an image.
Agents strengthen and abandon trails in a shared ground, asking how long neglected routes remain available and who chose the places worth connecting.
Crowds follow prepared arrows around obstacles or through wind, asking whether apparent agreement comes from neighbours or from decisions already written into the ground.
Three flocks negotiate separation, alignment and cohesion under different edges, asking who enters each agent’s neighbourhood and what this model of belonging omits.
Ants inherit fading trails from earlier populations, asking how shared memory and limited sensing shape routes that can look equally available from above.
Outward and returning ants leave different trails for later travellers, asking how reinforcement preserves some routes without proving that the strongest is optimal.
Particles change direction when their score changes, asking who defines improvement and how a limited archive decides which places count as novel.
Predators and prey continue through local encounters and population support, asking which recoveries arise within the ecosystem and which depend on an unseen caretaker.
Bodies rewarded for fresh ground exhaust their finite world, revealing selection and an unannounced ending inside a simulation presented as drift without a goal.
Three error landscapes judge the same observations differently, asking whether reducing an outlier’s influence corrects a mistake or suppresses evidence worth attending to.
Moving centres recolour stationary points and partition even an unstructured sample, asking when a geometric grouping is mistaken for a natural or named category.
A small network changes weighted connections through error, asking what its training history establishes and what remains unknown about cases it has never encountered.
Computed edges sit beside supplied object names and confidence scores, exposing the missing link between a real image operation and an unsupported recognition claim.
Hand-set gates make the same final token produce different outputs, asking what a memory retains, admits and reveals without claiming that this cell learns.
A scripted generator–critic diagram illustrates changing standards of success, asking what actual learning evidence is missing and which forms a reference set excludes.
Raised points make one anomaly rule visible, asking what its reference population calls unusual and what further evidence could justify investigating rather than discarding.
Two travellers visit the same graph in different orders, asking how queues and stacks distribute attention and how long an urgent destination must wait.
A graph’s drawing shifts while its connections stay fixed, asking whether apparent centrality belongs to the structure or only to position and viewpoint.
A spark reroutes as stepping stones disappear, asking which alternatives the graph permits and why a failed search cannot rule out another kind of crossing.
Authored hierarchies meet a fictional network of traceable records, asking what evidence supports a conspicuous vertex, a connection or a claim of importance.
Directed paths gather into groups with ways back, asking which extra connection would make return possible and what strong connectivity still cannot guarantee.
A minimum spanning tree saves connection cost by removing cycles, asking whose journeys lengthen and which discarded route would matter when an edge fails.
Junctions accumulate excess in a forward-only flow study, asking when a blocked allocation needs revision rather than being mistaken for an impossible network.
The same ring yields three or five pairs under different scan orders, asking when valid choices must be undone and what pair counts cannot judge.
A highlighted postulate, uneven parallels and unmeasured angle labels expose how the room makes assumptions feel obvious before their claims have been examined.
Triangles acquire different angle sums under different geometric hosts, asking what straightness depends on and why a convincing bend alone does not define another space.
Both membership choices contradict an unrestricted set rule, asking which restrictions enable a construction and how contradiction differs from an expectation that merely fails.
A jamming proof sculpture and rising tower picture arithmetic’s formal limits, asking what their displays establish and which assumptions an unprovability claim requires.
Staircases return their borrowed height and separated beams meet only in projection, asking where a persuasive local view fails to supply a consistent whole.
A row waits for the visitor’s next choice beside constructed witnesses, asking what finite evidence establishes and what a claim about every continuation still requires.
Conflicting door reports remain visible while passage continues, asking what follows from disagreement and who decides access before every account has been settled.
A proposed formula, branching recurrence and miniature room gather different limits, asking whose possibilities a model sustains and whether its inhabitants can challenge its terms.
Different control arrangements produce the same formula total, asking which distinctions a summary loses and what the model’s available terms teach its maker to overlook.
A bit grid separates source uncertainty from a predictor’s mistakes, asking whether difficulty belongs to the world or to the expectation brought to it.
A branching fan multiplies and prunes possible endings, asking who specified its options and why a larger count does not by itself mean more freedom.
A movable lit strip recommends a route through regular and dispersed forms, asking which preferences remain built into the architecture after the recommendation changes.
A signed rail acquires the labels resist and embrace beside an independent moving pattern, asking why direction and change do not establish improvement.
Two reaction–diffusion screens share a start and model time but take different steps, asking which patterns belong to the model and which to its calculation.
A reactor receives or retains slider values as their connection opens and closes, asking where a gesture actually reaches and what disconnection leaves behind.
A contained specimen changes stiffness, pressure and damping, asking what stability means and which possibilities remain fixed by the jar, mappings and maker’s expectations.
Compressed labels remain present but become harder to distinguish, asking whose differences a spatial representation preserves and whether its chosen groups repeat the flattening.
Tables, chairs and empty walls distribute invitations before anyone speaks, asking how geometry and colour propose participation without establishing equal access or a fair conversation.
Two branches remain, overlap or resolve into one shortened account, asking what settlement removes and which records would let that decision be reconsidered.
Four assigned verdicts and differently timed museum views expose their sources, asking what evidence, criteria and moment would make each partial account answerable.
A growing shared form counts arrivals, sources and revisions, asking what evidence and disagreement must survive for accumulated contributions to become knowledge people can revise.
A growing model and a walkable cave offer different connections, asking where returns are possible and which boundaries a visitor still cannot alter.
An editable body keeps changed poses and neighbours beside bodies that fall, asking how names, destinations and constraining connections shape what an arrangement can become.
A changed body returns beside its beginning, asking what saved positions and connections preserve, which gestures disappear and what another kind of return would require.
